speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand your bleeding issues, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been occurring and if there is any family history of bleeding disorders? I would also like to know if you have noticed any unusual bruising or bleeding after minor injuries.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any recent viral illnesses, high fevers, or bone pain, and have you noticed any bleeding from the gastrointestinal or urinary tracts? I would also like to know if there is any family history of bleeding disorders or if the child has been taking any new medications recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: To differentiate between a primary platelet disorder like ITP and a clotting factor deficiency, I need to assess for joint or muscle bleeding. Does the child have any history of deep tissue bruising, bleeding into joints (hemarthrosis), or excessive bleeding after minor cuts that takes more than 10 minutes to stop? speaker: Doctor
text: Since the platelet count is normal, we must look for a qualitative platelet defect or a coagulation factor issue. Does the child have any history of bleeding into joints (hemarthrosis) or deep muscle hematomas, and are there any other family members with similar bleeding symptoms? REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time_and_Coagulation_Profile

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bleeding_Time: Prolonged. Coagulation_Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal)

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged bleeding time with normal platelet count and coagulation profile strongly suggests a platelet function defect like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome. Does the child have a history of bleeding after minor trauma or dental work, and is there any family history of similar bleeding disorders? REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Aggregation_Study

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ELISA Binding Assay: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of GIIb/IIIa receptors confirms the diagnosis of Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's thrombasthenia
